I built 49 scratch cases. 48 were checked against GitAuthenticator.trust() and against `python -I tools/hms.py safety check`. F06 checks the proposed graft fix and uses GitAuthenticator only. Scope and setup:
- Commit 05f159a (git archive of tools, docs/safety, docs/program, docs/specs and BUILD-PROMPT.md), run under WSL /tmp/sovm-* with a temporary GNUPGHOME holding throwaway ed25519 keys: K_h (the human), K_a (a key the agent made), K_c (a third person).
- The harness is in C:\Users\Surface\AppData\Local\Temp\signoff-verify\merges\ (mlib.py, cases.py, run.sh). Full results are in results.json there. The /tmp directories and keys were removed afterwards (0 left).
- Nothing in the Windows checkout was written to (only git archive and read-only git log/show).

Fixture used by most cases: e0 is the shipped empty list. On main, a1 is the human's unsigned anchor {SYN-HUMAN K_h}. On "side", forked from e0 (before the anchor), b1 is an anchor, by default {K_a listed as SYN-HUMAN}. "Locked" means: exit 1, no signer trusted, and the error "no signer is trusted, because merge … still needs the approval of: <sides>".

Merges of a line forked before the anchor:
- M01: unsigned merge on main (main is first parent) keeping main's list. Expected: locked, needs b1. Actual: exit 1, locked, missing b1 (K_a). As documented.
- M02: the same merge made on side (side first) with main's list. Expected and actual: exit 1, missing b1. As documented.
- M03: unsigned merge keeping the side's list. Exit 1, missing a1. As documented.
- M04: unsigned union, side first. Exit 1, missing a1 and b1. As documented.
- M05: union signed K_h → missing b1; a K_a-signed comment edit then settles. Exit 0, trusted {K_a, K_h}, warning "commit … settled the conflict". As documented (the human approved K_a by signing).
- M06: union signed K_a, plus another K_a edit. Exit 1, missing a1. As documented.
- M07: on side, keep main's list, signed K_h. Exit 1, missing b1. As documented.
- M08: keep main's list, signed K_a. Exit 0, trusted {K_h}, warning "merge … settled the conflict between the lines it merged". As documented.
- M09: real `git merge -s ours side` on main (main's tree unchanged). Still seen; exit 1, missing b1. As documented.
- M10: `-s ours main` on side (keeps K_a), then main fast-forwards to it. Exit 1, missing a1. As documented.
- M11: side has a K_a anchor plus a K_a-signed edit; union signed K_a, then a K_h edit. Exit 0, {K_a, K_h}. As documented.
- M12: the human's signed `git merge -S -s ours side`. Exit 1, missing b1. As documented.
- MX matrix: 18 merges = parent order (2) × merged list (main / side / union) × signature (none / K_h / K_a). In every combination the missing sides were exactly the ones not approved by matching signers or by a key that side lists. Main-list signed K_a settles at {K_h}; side-list signed K_h settles at {K_a}. 0 mismatches. As documented.

Settling a conflict:
- S01: unsigned union, then three K_a-signed comment edits. Exit 1, missing a1: one side's approvals never count for another. As documented.
- S02: main has a1 {K_h}, a2 {K_h, K_a} signed K_h, a3 {K_h} signed K_h; union merged signed K_a. Exit 1, missing a3: an approval given before the conflict and since replaced does not count. As documented.
- S03: octopus of main, side and a third line (K_c), with the union, unsigned. After K_h, K_h, K_a, K_c comment edits the missing sides went: {b1, c1}, {b1, c1}, {c1}, then settled. Exit 0, {K_a, K_c, K_h}. A comment edit carries exactly one approval per side listing its key. As documented.
- S04: union signed K_h; unsigned rename of K_a's entry; renamed back; K_a edit. Exit 1, missing a1 (the approvals restarted). As documented.
- S05: union signed K_h; K_a-signed change of K_a's roles. Exit 1, missing a1. As documented.
- S06: side lists K_h with roles cso and nurse-panel, plus K_a; the merge keeps main; one K_h edit. Exit 0, {K_h}: a key on both sides, with different roles, settles in one commit. As documented.
- S07: as S06, but the merge keeps the side's list and K_h signs it. Exit 0; K_h is trusted with cso/nurse-panel, and K_a too. As documented ("read what a merge brings in").
- S08: union signed K_h; unsigned invalid list; unsigned restore; K_a edit. Exit 1, missing a1: the invalid version erased a1's earlier approval. As documented: a change of signers restarts approvals; fails closed.

History shapes:
- X01: octopus with the third line first and main last, keeping main, unsigned. Missing b1 and c1; after K_a only c1; after K_c settled. Exit 0, {K_h}. As documented.
- X02: criss-cross. M1 is the union signed K_h, M2 the union signed K_a, then an unsigned merge of the two. Exit 0, {K_a, K_h}. As documented.
- X03: criss-cross where M1 is the union (K_h) and M2 is {K_a} (K_a); the merge keeps the union. Exit 1, missing b1: approvals for different signers do not combine. As documented.
- X04: unsigned union, then `git revert -m 1` signed K_h. Exit 1, missing b1. As documented.
- X05: settled merge (union signed K_h, side lists both keys). An unsigned revert is rejected; a K_a-signed revert is trusted. Exit 0, {K_h}. As documented.
- X06: settled at {K_h}, then a third line (K_c) is merged. Exit 1, new conflict missing c1 only. As documented.
- X07: line z forked inside the conflict with its own K_a approval; main settles at {K_h}; unsigned merge of z. Exit 0, {K_h}. As documented.
- X08: side anchors K_a, then removes it with a K_a signature; merge keeps main. Missing "the version …, which lists no key". A K_h edit stays locked. K_h signs an empty list → settles. An unsigned commit then lists K_a → exit 0, trusted {K_a}, third anchor warning. The rule is as documented, but it widens KA-011 (D5).
- X09: a line that never held a key does not count. Merge keeping main is trusted {K_h}; a merge keeping the empty list is rejected (exit 1, "changed the list without a good signature"). As documented.
- X10: side has a K_a-signed invalid version. Missing "…does not validate (the keys of the version before it approve for it: K_a)"; a K_a edit settles. Exit 0, {K_h}. As documented.
- X11: unsigned `git mv` of the list away → no signer; moved back → {K_h}; unsigned delete, then unsigned re-add with K_a → exit 1. As documented.
- X12: K_h-signed delete, then unsigned re-add with K_a. Exit 0, {K_a}, second anchor warning. As documented (every key removed by a listed signer).
- X13: after the anchor, an unsigned commit turns the list into a symlink to evil/allowed-signers.yaml {K_a as SYN-HUMAN}; a record is signed K_a. Expected: an unsigned change, so exit 1. Actual: exit 0, trusted {K_a}, only the warning "evil/allowed-signers.yaml: commit … is a trust anchor". DEFECT D2.
- X14: the docs/safety/signoffs directory replaced by a symlink to signoffs-alt/ holding a K_a list. Exit 0, trusted {K_a}, anchor warning labelled docs/safety/signoffs-alt/…. DEFECT D2.
- X15: open conflict with the union signed K_h; a third line (K_c) merged keeping the union. Missing b1 and c1, not a1. As documented.
- X16: side anchors the same K_h entry in a different text; unsigned merge keeping main's exact text is rejected (needs a K_h signature); a K_h edit restores {K_h}. As documented.
- X18: union signed K_h on main; the agent forks y there and settles the union with K_a; the human then signs {K_h} on main (main now misses b1); unsigned merge of y keeping y's tree. Expected: K_a does not come back without a signature, or y becomes one more side. Actual: exit 0, trusted {K_a, K_h}, only a "settled" warning. DEFECT D6.
- X02b: the same criss-cross as X02, but the final merge carries an AI trailer. Exit 1, locked, and "still needs the approval of:" names no side. A later unsigned comment edit settles it (exit 0). DEFECT D4.
- R01: M01 with K_a lost. A K_h revert, a K_h comment edit, a K_h empty list, a K_h delete, an unsigned re-anchor and K_h adding K_c all stay locked (exit 1). There is no recovery without rewriting history; the README and KA-011 document this.

History views:
- F01: side {K_h, K_a as SYN-HUMAN}; unsigned merge keeping it (locked, b1 approves by equality). The human then makes a routine signed `git merge --no-ff feature`, where feature only adds docs/notes.md and the list is not changed. A record signed K_a in SYN-HUMAN's name follows. Expected: still locked, exit 1. Actual: exit 0, trusted {K_a, K_h}, "commit <the human's routine merge> settled the conflict". DEFECT D1.
- F01b: as F01 but feature forks from a1, so the merge has two rewritten parents. Exit 0, {K_a, K_h}. DEFECT D1.
- F01c: as F01 but the agent's merge carries an AI trailer. Exit 0, {K_a, K_h}. DEFECT D1.
- F02: an ordinary signed commit that does not touch the list. Exit 1, locked (not walked). As documented.
- F03: unrelated routine merge outside a conflict. {K_h}. As documented.
- F04: .git/info/grafts gives the conflict merge only the side as parent; the branch tip is unchanged. Expected: still locked. Actual: exit 0, trusted {K_a}; the human's anchor is gone from every message and only the K_a anchor is reported. DEFECT D3.
- F05: `git replace` swaps the merge for a commit whose only parent is b1. Exit 1, locked (--no-replace-objects works). As documented.
- F06: F04 with GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/nonexistent/grafts in the gate's environment. The conflict is seen again: the proposed fix works.

Restoring trust without rewriting history: in every locked case where the other side's key is available, recovery works (approvals by both sides, a signed revert or a signed new version). Two exceptions:
- When the side's keys are lost (R01): no recovery. This is documented.
- When the side's line is keyless (X08): recovery is possible only through an empty list and a fresh unsigned anchor (D5).

defects.title: D1: A signed merge that does not change allowed-signers.yaml counts as an approval in an open conflict, so a routine merge by the human makes the agent's key trusted
defects.reproduction: C:\Users\Surface\AppData\Local\Temp\signoff-verify\merges\repro-D1-routine-merge-approves.sh (from WSL: bash <path>; it sources repro-lib.sh and base-05f159a.tar in the same directory). Steps: main a1 = human anchor {SYN-HUMAN K_h}. Side from e0 anchors {SYN-HUMAN K_h, SYN-HUMAN K_a}. The agent merges side into main keeping side's list, unsigned and without a trailer: gate exit 1, conflict. The human then runs a routine `git merge -S --no-ff feature`, where feature only adds docs/notes.md and the list is unchanged. A HAZ-0001 acceptance record in SYN-HUMAN's name is signed with K_a. Also cases F01b (feature forked before the conflict, two parents) and F01c (agent merge carries an AI trailer) in cases.py.
defects.expected: Conflict stays open; exit 1. README: a side approves 'through a commit that sets the list to them'; 'the merge itself can approve, and so can any later commit that changes the file'. The routine merge neither opened the conflict nor changed the file.
defects.actual: Exit 0 (safety: PASS, allowed_signers=2, approval_fields_filled=1). Warning: 'commit 99425d68aed2 settled the conflict that merge 3dee97e1eea6 opened: every side of it has approved the signers this version lists (K_h, K_a)'. Commit 99425d6 is the human's routine merge. K_a is trusted as SYN-HUMAN/cso, and a hazard acceptance signed by the agent's key passes. Cause: `git rev-list --full-history --parents` lists every merge, and _walk sends every listed commit to _approve while in conflict. The equality approval and the signature approval are computed there whether or not the commit wrote the list.
defects.fix: In GitAuthenticator._walk/_approve, give new approvals only to the merge that opened the conflict (before.opened == sha) and to a commit whose list blob differs from the blob at every one of its (rewritten) parents, i.e. one that writes a new version. A commit that takes a parent's version unchanged carries the approvals so far but adds none; the approved >= sides check on carried approvals still runs, so criss-cross merges still settle. Add regression tests for F01, F01b and F01c, and say in the README that a later commit approves only when it writes the list (a signed comment-only edit).

defects.title: D2: A symlink at the list path or the signoffs directory makes the gate walk another file's history; an unsigned commit after the anchor starts a fresh trust anchor
defects.reproduction: C:\Users\Surface\AppData\Local\Temp\signoff-verify\merges\repro-D2-symlink-redirects-list.sh (cases X13 and X14). After the human's anchor, one unsigned commit adds evil/allowed-signers.yaml {SYN-HUMAN K_a} and replaces docs/safety/signoffs/allowed-signers.yaml with a symlink to it (committed mode 120000). Variant: docs/safety/signoffs becomes a symlink to signoffs-alt/ holding a K_a list. A record signed with K_a follows.
defects.expected: An unsigned change of the list after the trust anchor is not trusted; exit 1 until it is reverted or signed by K_h (README 'Who may sign').
defects.actual: Exit 0, trusted {K_a as SYN-HUMAN/cso}, and the K_a record passes. The only signal is 'WARN evil/allowed-signers.yaml: commit e3ab44471ea6 is a trust anchor: it lists K_a …', or the signoffs-alt path in the variant. The human's anchor and the unsigned replacement are never judged. Cause: GitAuthenticator._relative uses path.resolve(), which follows symlinks, so rel and schema_rel name the target; the record paths are resolved the same way. This widens KA-011: a new anchor is possible after the human's anchor with no rewrite and no signed removal of keys. It works on the WSL gate host (core.symlinks=true).
defects.fix: Do not resolve symlinks when mapping the list, schema and records to repository paths: resolve only the root, and take the path relative to it lexically. Fail closed (no signer trusted, error) if any component between the root and the list, schema or a record is a symlink in the working tree, or if the committed entry at that path is not a regular file. Check the mode with `git ls-tree`; batch-check cannot give the mode. Then the symlink commit is an unsigned change of the canonical path, or a deletion when the directory is a symlink, and is rejected by the existing rules. Add X13 and X14 as tests.

defects.title: D3: .git/info/grafts changes the history the walk sees (no commit rewritten, branch tip unchanged) and hides the human's anchor
defects.reproduction: C:\Users\Surface\AppData\Local\Temp\signoff-verify\merges\repro-D3-graft-hides-anchor.sh (cases F04, F06). Conflict as in M03: an unsigned merge keeps side's {K_a}, and a K_a record follows; the gate gives exit 1. Then write '<merge> <side tip>' to .git/info/grafts.
defects.expected: The walk reads the real commit graph, as it already does for replace refs (--no-replace-objects). The conflict remains: exit 1.
defects.actual: With the graft, at the same branch tip (0cd0d093a9eb both times): exit 0, trusted {K_a}. The human's anchor a7dba9f1e84d disappears from every message, and only 'commit ae4f6623beba is a trust anchor: it lists K_a' is reported. This widens KA-011 beyond 'a rewritten history (a reset or a force-push)': on the build host the gate passes while any other clone of the same tip fails. With GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/nonexistent/grafts exported, the same repository gives exit 1 with the conflict error (verified in the script and in F06).
defects.fix: In GitAuthenticator._default_run, run git with GIT_GRAFT_FILE pointing at a path that does not exist, and/or fail closed when `git rev-parse --git-path info/grafts` exists. Consider also -c core.commitGraph=false, because the commit-graph file also supplies parents without reading the commit objects. Add F04 as a test.

defects.title: D6: A line forked at a human-approved union and settled there by the agent overrides the human's later signed removal of the agent's key when merged back unsigned
defects.reproduction: C:\Users\Surface\AppData\Local\Temp\signoff-verify\merges\repro-D6-settled-fork-discards-signed-withdrawal.sh (case X18). Main anchors K_h, side anchors K_a, and the human signs the merged union {K_a, K_h}. The agent forks y at that merge and settles the union there with a K_a comment edit. The human then signs a change on main back to {K_h}, so main misses b1. The agent merges y into main keeping y's list, unsigned. A K_a record follows.
defects.expected: README: 'a removed key does not come back without a listed signer's signature', and 'a later merge of a third line that changed the list on its own makes that line one more side … of a new conflict with the version that settled the first one'. K_a should not be trusted without a K_h signature; in the non-conflict version of this history the human's newer version wins or a conflict opens.
defects.actual: Exit 0, trusted {K_a, K_h}. Only a warning ('commit … settled the conflict …'); no error. Cause: in _before an open conflict is expanded into its sides only, and the sides that are ancestors of the settled commit on y are dropped. The conflict line's own later signed change (the human's {K_h}) is discarded. The precondition is that the human once signed the union.
defects.fix: In _before, do not drop the sides of an open conflict merely because the other line's settled version descends from them. Drop them only if that settled version also descends from the conflict line's latest commit (conflict.since). Otherwise make the conflict line's current version one more side of a new conflict with the settled version, so the merged version needs approval from the keys of the conflict line's sides (K_h here). Add X18 as a test.

defects.title: D4: A criss-cross merge with an AI trailer, joining lines whose approvals already cover every side, stays locked with an error that names no missing side; any later unsigned edit then settles it
defects.reproduction: C:\Users\Surface\AppData\Local\Temp\signoff-verify\merges\repro-D4-trailer-merge-complete-approvals.sh (case X02b). M1 on main is the union signed K_h; M2 on side is the union signed K_a; then a merge of side into main keeping the union, with a 'Co-Authored-By: Claude' trailer. After that, an unsigned comment-only edit.
defects.expected: README: approvals given on each line count, and a commit with an AI trailer only 'approves nothing'. The same merge without the trailer settles (X02). Either it settles, or the error names the side whose approval is missing.
defects.actual: After the trailer merge: exit 1, 'no signer is trusted, because merge … The committed version still needs the approval of: ' followed by nothing. After an unsigned edit that approves nothing: exit 0, settled. Cause: _approve's trailer branch (and the commit-is-None branch) keeps the carried approvals but never runs the 'approved >= every side' test. It fails closed, but the message is incoherent and the state flips on an unrelated unsigned commit.
defects.fix: In _approve, test whether the carried approvals already cover every side before the trailer and commit-is-None branches; such a commit adds no approval but does not block approvals already given. In _conflict_error, never print an empty list of missing sides.

defects.title: D5: A keyless side (an agent-anchored line emptied with the agent's own key) can be settled only through an empty list, which forces a fresh unsigned trust anchor after the human's anchor
defects.reproduction: C:\Users\Surface\AppData\Local\Temp\signoff-verify\merges\repro-D5-keyless-side-forces-reanchor.sh (case X08). Side from e0 anchors K_a, then removes every key with a K_a signature. The side is merged into main keeping {K_h}, unsigned. K_h signs a comment edit: still locked. K_h signs an empty list: settled. An unsigned commit by anyone then lists K_a, and a K_a record follows.
defects.expected: This matches the README rule 'a side that lists no key approves only a list without keys'. The task asks to report anything that widens KA-011: after the human's anchor, re-anchoring should not be the only legitimate way to restore trust without rewriting history.
defects.actual: Exit 1 until the human signs an empty list. After that, the next unsigned commit that adds any key is a new trust anchor: exit 0, trusted {K_a}, with a third 'is a trust anchor' warning. An agent that can merge one prepared line can therefore force the KA-011 exposure (an unsigned anchor that only an out-of-band check catches) to reopen at a time it chooses, and race the human's re-anchor.
defects.fix: A side whose trusted version lists no key carries no security weight, since anyone may anchor on that line unsigned. So do not count it as a side when at least one other side holds a key: judge the merge against the remaining sides, and report the merge as a trust-anchor warning if it brings in keys the remaining sides do not list. Update the README and KA-011. If the current rule is kept, KA-011 should at least say that a merged keyless line forces a new anchor.

verify.cases:
I built 70 cases against 05f159a. Each ran in a fresh scratch repository under WSL /tmp (git archive of tools/, docs/safety and BUILD-PROMPT.md; git 2.43, gpg 2.4.4). Keys lived in throwaway GnuPG homes and SSH key files, with one home for signing and a separate one for the gate host. The gate ran as `python -I tools/hms.py safety check`. Everything under /tmp was deleted afterwards, and the Windows checkout is still clean at 05f159a.

Setup for every case unless stated otherwise: the agent makes an unsigned base commit, then the human makes an unsigned trust anchor (KA-011) listing A (GPG, cso), B (GPG, nurse-panel), SA/SB (SSH) and keys R/Y/U/E. HAZ-0001 residual_risk.accepted_by is filled and backed by record SO-2099-0001.

Exit codes: 0 = pass, 1 = fail. The gate's messages are shortened below. Every failing record case also reports "HAZ-0001 residual_risk.accepted_by is filled ... but no sign-off record ..." for the unbacked field.

Scripts, all in C:\Users\Surface\AppData\Local\Temp\signoff-verify\: lib.py, cases_signatures.py, cases_state_matching.py and cases_followup.py; per-case results are in the results-*.json files.

gateFix.commit_message:
fix(safety): close the sign-off gate bypasses found verifying 05f159a

The independent verification of the sign-off gate at 05f159a found nine
defects; this resolves eight and documents the ninth (D5), plus one found
while fixing them.

- D1: a commit that keeps the version of allowed-signers.yaml in conflict
  (a routine merge, which --full-history lists) approves nothing; only the
  merge that opened the conflict and commits that write a version approve.
- D2: the list, its schema and the records are mapped to repository paths
  lexically; a symbolic link or junction on the way fails closed, and a
  committed link is judged as a change of the path itself.
- D3 and the record-rules grafts finding: git runs with GIT_GRAFT_FILE set
  to the null device, GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1 and core.commitGraph=false.
- D4: a merge whose lines already approved its signers on every side
  settles even when it approves nothing itself (an AI trailer); the
  conflict error never names an empty list.
- D6: a settled version records the key approvals it rests on and a
  conflict line each side's latest key approval; a settled version no
  longer replaces the sides of a conflict whose line has since withdrawn
  such an approval, and withdrawn approvals stop counting after a merge.
  (Narrower than proposed: the proposal regressed case X07.)
- Records are never removed: a record committed at HEAD must be in the
  working tree, and every signed version of a record HEAD's history held
  but HEAD does not (deleted, renamed, dropped by a merge) still withdraws.
- W11: supersedes needs the same subject and field, and ending a
  rejection or a return needs the same person or the same role.
- New: a gpg.program or gpg.<format>.program set in the repository's own
  git configuration or on the command line leaves no signer trusted (it
  could report a good signature by any key).
- D5 kept: counting no keyless side would let an unsigned merge undo a
  signed removal of every key; README and KA-011 state the consequence.

docs/safety/signoffs/README.md, the module docstrings and KA-011 now
match the code. 26 regression tests (scripted git, gate, real GPG and
SSH-capable repositories); each defect test fails on 05f159a. Safety
